findings.title: Test does not join the reader thread before asserting
findings.body: The test starts a reader thread but never calls `join()` on it. After `deletedAll.set(true)`, the main thread immediately asserts `caughtExceptions` is empty. However, the reader thread may still be in the middle of an HTTP request at that point. This means the assertion can pass even if the reader thread would have caught an exception, making the test unreliable (false negatives). A `thread.join()` should be called before the assertion.

findings.title: Other modelSupplier.get() call sites still lack null checks
findings.body: The fix adds a null check for `modelSupplier.get()` in `getSubGroupsCount()` (line 274), but the same pattern exists without null checks in `getSubGroupsStream(String search, Integer firstResult, Integer maxResults)` (line 256), `getSubGroupsStream(Integer firstResult, Integer maxResults)` (line 262), and `getSubGroupsStream(String search, Boolean exact, Integer firstResult, Integer maxResults)` (line 268). If the group is deleted concurrently, these methods will still throw an NPE when `modelSupplier.get()` returns null, which is the exact scenario this PR aims to fix.

findings.title: Test may not reliably exercise the concurrent read-during-delete scenario
findings.body: The reader thread is started and then the main thread immediately begins deleting all 100 groups. There is no synchronization to ensure the reader thread has actually made at least one request before deletions begin. If the deletion loop completes before the reader thread's first HTTP call is issued, the test passes trivially without ever exercising the race condition it is designed to detect. Consider using a latch or verifying at least one read occurred before starting deletions.
